results.text:
I learned most of this by screwing it up. Some of it I just thought through, and I’m still not sure about all of it.

Before making love, I want to know enough about the hard stuff that I’m not finding it all out after I’m bonded. Jealousy, attraction to other people, what happens under stress, old patterns, how recent the healing is, what each of us wants when things go bad, money. But asking, “How do you handle jealousy?” can get me a beautiful answer that tells me almost nothing. I’d rather ask what she thinks she would do in an actual situation.

I can learn a lot by talking, but there's a point where more questions mostly teach me what the person says about themself. After that I need ordinary time. Ten profound conversations in one weekend may tell me we can have profound conversations. They don't tell me what she's like on a boring day, or when she's annoyed and doesn't have an answer prepared.

results.text:
I'd also try to make some real friends together. My friends are going to hear me first and hers are going to hear her first. That's normal; they're our friends. The problem is when every person around the relationship only knows one of us well. Then the first serious conflict turns into two teams arguing about two different relationships.

And don't stop your own practices just because you're in love. If I stop reparenting and meditating because my partner makes me feel okay, then she's doing part of that job for me whether we say so or not.
